question: Explain the concept of 'lifting the corporate veil'. State the situations in which the courts or the law may disregard the separate legal entity of a company.
sources: Salomon v. Salomon & Co. Ltd. (separate legal entity)
Gilford Motor Co. v. Horne (sham company)
Daimler Co. Ltd. v. Continental Tyre and Rubber Co. (enemy character)
Companies Act, 2013 - provisions imposing personal liability (prospectus, fraudulent conduct of business)

points.label: Separate legal entity
points.description: A company is a legal person distinct from its members, as held in Salomon v. Salomon & Co. Ltd.; this separation is called the corporate veil.
points.basis: Salomon v. Salomon & Co. Ltd.; incorporation under the Companies Act, 2013

points.label: Meaning of lifting the veil
points.description: In some cases the courts or the statute ignore the separate entity and look at the persons behind the company, holding them personally responsible.
points.basis: Judicial and statutory exceptions to the separate entity principle

points.label: Fraud or sham company
points.description: Where the company is used as a cloak for fraud or to evade a legal obligation, e.g. Gilford Motor Co. v. Horne, where a company was set up to avoid a restraint of trade.

points.label: Enemy character and tax evasion
points.description: To decide whether a company is an enemy company by looking at who controls it (Daimler Co. Ltd. v. Continental Tyre and Rubber Co.), and where a company is formed only to evade tax.
points.basis: Daimler Co. Ltd. v. Continental Tyre and Rubber Co.; tax evasion cases

points.label: Statutory cases
points.description: The Act itself makes persons liable, e.g. for misstatements in a prospectus, for fraudulent conduct of business, and where business continues with fewer than the minimum members for more than six months.
points.basis: Companies Act, 2013, provisions imposing personal liability on directors, officers and members
